questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.**

I __told__ Rahu __on__ wait __for__ two hours __at__ the bus stop.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 4) i.e. 'on.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'on.'
 
• In the erroneous part, the use of the preposition** 'on'** is wrong as the verb** 'wait'** is in the base form.
 
• We need to use** 'to'** before the base form of the verb.
 
• The word **'to'** in the erroneous segment will be acting as part of the '**to-infinitive'. **The to-infinitive is formed as** 'to + base form of the verb'.**
 
• The **to-infinitive **is used in many sentence constructions, often expressing the purpose of something or someone's opinion about something.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *She told Anil **to eat **the burger.*
 
 
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'to' in place of 'on' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct sentence:__* **I told Rahu __**to**__ wait for two hours at the bus stop.*

questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence contains a grammatical error in the first segment, **"They was"**.
 
• The subject **"They"** is plural, and therefore, the correct verb form is **"were"**, not **"was"**.
 
• Correct grammar usage would be: **"They were"**.
 
• The other segments of the sentence are grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: *They were celebrating their Silver wedding anniversary next month in Dubai.*

• **Subject-verb agreement:** Always match the verb form to the subject in terms of number (singular or plural).

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.**

Bobo was / very richer than Jim / as he had illicitly accumulated / all his wealth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'very richer than Jim'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'richer'** is already in a comparative degree of adjective.
 
• So adding the adjective **'very'** before it is just redundant.
 
• Hence this part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *Bobo was richer than Jim as he had illicitly accumulated all his wealth.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **'Very' **can be used as an adverb (before adjectives and adverbs).
 
• **Example- **
 
 
• It had been a long day and he was **very** tired. 
 
• I always walk **very** quickly. 
 
• She writes **very** well. 
 
 
 
• It can also be used as an adjective (only before a noun).
 
 
• Example- They went down to the** very** bottom of the sea.

questions.question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains a grammatical error in the conditional clause "If I was a king."
 
• When expressing hypothetical or unreal situations, the verb "was" should be replaced with "were" in the clause following "if."
 
• The correct phrasing is "If I were a king," which aligns with the subjunctive mood used for hypothetical conditions.
 
• This correction ensures the sentence is grammatically accurate and conveys the intended meaning properly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"If I were a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "on my country"** – This is incorrect as the correct preposition to use is "from" in this context.
 
• **Option 2: "my best by remove poverty"** – This is grammatically incorrect as "by remove" should be replaced with "by removing."
 
• **Option 4: "I would has tried"** – This is grammatically incorrect as "has" should be replaced with "have" in this context.

questions.question:
Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence.

She sings good.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **well**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"good"** means having the required qualities, or of a high standard. (अच्छा)

 
 
• **Example: **She is a good person who always helps others.
 
 
 
• **"Well" **refers to performing an action in a good or satisfactory way. It is the adverb form used to describe how an action is performed. (अच्छी तरह)
 
 
• **Example: **She sings well in the choir.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct word to use in the sentence is **'well'** instead of **'good'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. well**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Better **(बेहतर): Comparative form of good, meaning of a higher standard or quality.

 
 
• **Example:** Her singing has improved and is much better now.
 
 
 
• **Best **(सर्वोत्तम): Superlative form of good, meaning of the highest quality.
 
 
• **Example: **She is the best singer in the competition.
 
 
 
• **Goodly** (विशाल): An archaic or literary term meaning large in size or quantity.
 
 
• **Example:** He donated a goodly sum to charity.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Our team have won the match.
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is "**have**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of the verb "**have**" is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the **subject-verb agreement** is incorrect.
 
• The **collective noun **is always followed by a **singular verb **as collective nouns are taken as one unit or group.
 
• In the given sentence, the collective noun "**team**"(subject) should be used with the singular verb "**has**".
 
• If the subject of the sentence was referring to individual members of a group then we use the plural verb "**have**":
 
 
• **Example**: *The members of the parliament **have **__decided to implement the policy.*
 
 

**The correct sentence is**:* Our team __**has **__won the match.*

Hence, the correct answer is** option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** 

 
• We use the verb generally "**have**" for two reasons.
 
• To show the possession of something
 
 
• **Example**: *I have a sports car.*
 
 
 
• As an auxiliary verb when performing an action
 
 
• **Example**: *I have an important meeting today.*

questions.question: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.

options.text: I hope your health is getting better by next week.
I hope your health will get better by next week.
I hope your health have been getting better by next week.
I hope your health is get better by next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Future Tense: **The phrase** "will get better" **correctly uses **the future tense **to describe **an improvement in health that is expected to happen by next week.**
 
• **Verb Agreement:** The future tense is formed by using** "will"** before the base form of the verb, which in this case is **"get."**
 
• **Clarity of Intention:** Using **"will**" shows a clear intention or expectation of future improvement, which aligns with the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Context Appropriateness:** The context of the sentence is about something expected to happen in the future, making** "will get better"** the most appropriate choice.
 
• **Hope and Expectation:** The phrase** "I hope"** sets the expectation, and** "will get better"** fits logically as it refers to a future event that is hoped for.
 
• **Common Usage:** This construction is commonly used in English to express hope for future improvements or changes.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Uses present continuous tense **"is getting,"** which is incorrect for a future expectation.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect usage of **"have been getting,"** which is present perfect continuous tense, not appropriate for future hope.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect grammar as **"is get" **doesn't form a valid verb phrase.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

He was surprised at me refusing his offer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__at me refusing__**

**__*Key Points__**

 
• **'at my refusing' **should be there in place of **'at me refusing'**
 
• **Possessive case of pronoun **comes before gerund for the following reason:
 
 
• The failure to use the possessive case with the gerund can create an illogical statement
 
• Consider the following sentence:
 
 
• I appreciate you taking time to talk with me about the project.

 ​The possessive case of *you* is not used with the gerund *taking*, so the writer ends up making the illogical statement (at least in this context) “I appreciate you.” The point is not that the writer of the sentence appreciates you,* per se; instead, the writer appreciates the fact that you took time to discuss the project: ​​
 
• I appreciate *your* taking time to talk with me about the project.​​​​​​
 
 
 
 

**Thus, the correct sentence is:* ****He was surprised at my refusing his offer.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

What are the __options available of me__ for a change of career?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'options available to me'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'options available to me'** should be used instead of** 'options available of me'.**
 
• The **adjective** '**available**' should be followed by '**to**' in the given context.
 
• It means '(used about things) that you can get, buy, use, etc. उपलब्‍ध, (वस्‍तुएँ)'.
 
 
• *Example: This information is easily **available to** everyone at the local library.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *What are the **options available to** me fir a change of career?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य **व्याकरण** की दृष्टि से **गलत** है।
 
• यहाँ, 'options available of me'. के स्थान पर 'options available to me' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• दिए गए संदर्भ में **adjective** 'available' के बाद '**to**' होना चाहिए।

• Therefore, **option 4** is the correct answer.

**Correct Sentence:** *People **have been warned** in advance about the coming economic crisis.*
